Article Title: 'Cops everywhere': Wife Gitanjali shares photo from hospital, claims Wangchuk under constant vigil
Article Text:
Gitanjali said the cops have been deciding who "may or may not meet him".

NEW DELHI: Gitanjali J Angmo, Sonam Wangchuk 's wife, claimed the activist has been under constant vigil, saying "police are everywhere", be it at the reception, in the lifts or outside the ICU.She said the cops have been deciding who "may or may not meet him", questioning whether the authorities were defying the court's order on his detention."At both Safdarjung and now Medanta, police are everywhere. At the main gate. The reception. The lifts. Outside@Wangchuk66’s ICU. They decide who may or may not meet him. If the Court has clarified that he is not under detention, then under what authority is this happening?" Gitanjali wrote on X.She further wrote: "In an enlightened democracy, is the role of the police to protect citizens and uphold the law, or to control citizens on behalf of those in power? These are questions every Indian should be asking."Meanwhile, Sonam Wangchuk, hours after he ended his 26-day hunger strike in the presence of Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, said he made the decision only after he got assurances from the govt and MPs across party lines that his demands for exam reforms and no action against peaceful protesters would be met.In a video posted on X early Friday, Wangchuk said he extended his fast by two days as negotiations with the Centre were under way and he finally got a written assurance.“End of hunger... Beginning of accountability,” Wangchuk posted on X, sharing a video explaining his decision to end the hunger strike. “Negotiations were on for these assurances since the last two days, for which I had to extend my hunger strike. I could have extended it further if required,” he said.After Wangchuk broke his fast, Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke posted on X: “We are relieved and grateful that Sonam sir has ended his hunger strike after 26 days. Thank you, sir, for your extraordinary courage and sacrifice. By putting your own life on the line, you awakened the conscience of an entire nation. Your life is far too precious to this country. The Cockroach Janta Party’s peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar will continue until Dharmendra Pradhan resigns. ”Wangchuk said in his post that he ended the fast after getting assurance from the government and MPs of all political parties that the issue of accountability in the ‘failing’ examination system would be discussed in Parliament.The engineer and climate activist broke his fast with juice a little after 12.30 am Friday and followed it up with a bowl of chicken soup as part of the initial phase of nutritional rehabilitation, according to sources in Medanta.“After 26 days, this tastes very good, but hunger doesn’t taste bad either. My doctors here have been very, very kind,” he said from his hospital bed, surrounded by doctors, the ministers and his wife Gitanjali J Angmo.He said 65 MPs from different political parties had extended support to his campaign and that he insisted on a written commitment after two days of discussions with the Centre.“Both the ruling party and MPs from the opposition have assured me their discussions will happen on thefloor of Parliament regarding reforms in the examination system like NEET and others, and that we will also be discussing the accountability of such lapses. And that we will make sure such things never happen… You will take accountability in the ministry with the minister also as a responsibility, and I’m sure you are already considering.And with these assurances, I’m touched and grateful to govt, and I want to appeal to the protesting students to maintain utmost peace. To express their feelings is a legitimate thing, but I do not approve violence of any kind, and allowing any antisocial elements to take advantage of this is not acceptable to me. It should be a genuine demand by genuinely concerned people, in this case youngsters. Sowith that being fulfilled, I'm grateful and I'll be happy to break my fast,” he says in the video.
Article Summary: Gitanjali J Angmo, Sonam Wangchuk's wife, claimed the activist has been under constant vigil. She said the cops have been deciding who "may or may not meet him" Wangchuk said he extended his fast by two days as negotiations with the Centre were under way.

Article Title: Delhi Police claims only 3,000 cops present for 10,000 protesters, file 15 FIRs
Article Text:
Delhi police uses facial recognition system at Jantar Mantar

NEW DELHI: Amid the ongoing student protest, Delhi police have deployed around 3,000 police personnel to maintain law and order for nearly 10,000 people present in and around Jantar Mantar.Police sources said around 130 police personnel have been injured and 15 FIRs have been registered in connection with the agitation, according to Delhi Police sources. The police also said around 65 students sustained injuries during the demonstrations.The Delhi Police further said it is using Facial Recognition System (FRS) cameras to identify "anti-social elements" visiting Jantar Mantar.According to police sources, more than 2,000 people with criminal records who had visited the protest site have been identified so far, as cited by ANI.This is not the first time the Delhi Police has deployed Facial Recognition System (FRS) cameras.The force has previously used the technology as part of security arrangements during Republic Day, Independence Day, Holi, Diwali, Eid, Ramlila celebrations and several other major public events across the city.Meanwhile, Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday said he has been diagnosed with typhoid but asserted that the nationwide protests demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan would continue without interruption.On Friday, Dipke welcomed activist Sonam Wangchuk's decision to end his 26-day hunger strike but reiterated that the movement would continue until its demand for accountability over the examination irregularities is met."Our demonstration will go on until Dharmendra Pradhan steps down. Any meeting must take place at a neutral location or venue. Nothing less than the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan will be accepted," he said.Meanwhile, activist Sonam Wangchuk responded to criticism over his decision to end his 26-day hunger strike held in support of students protesting the alleged NEET paper leak.In a video message shared on social media, Wangchuk questioned why his commitment to the cause required a "character certificate".Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike after receiving a written assurance from the Union government on the NEET examination issue and broader systemic reforms to the country's competitive examination framework.The activist said he had earlier been offered verbal assurances but insisted on a written commitment, which delayed the end of his fast by two days.Following a nearly two-hour meeting with Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, representatives of CJP said the government had sought time until Saturday afternoon to consider their demand for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
Article Summary: Delhi police deploy 3,000 police personnel to maintain law and order at Jantar Mantar. Police sources say around 130 police personnel have been injured and 15 FIRs have been registered. Delhi Police is using Facial Recognition System (FRS) cameras to identify "anti-social elements"

Article Title: Govt fact-checks viral AI deepfakes of PM, ministers; points to Pakistani handles
Article Text: NEW DELHI: The government has debunked doctored videos circulating on social media that wrongly showed Prime Minister Narendra Modi making threatening remarks against those protesting at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar over perpetual NEET paper leak. The Press Information Bureau (PIB) fact check unit said the clips were AI-generated deepfakes and did not reflect the Prime Minister’s actual statements.In related fact-checks, the government also flagged manipulated videos of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and commerce minister Piyush Goyal that were circulating on social media, falsely portraying them as making similar remarks against protesting students.In a post on X, the PIB fact check unit said, “Pakistani propaganda accounts are circulating a video of Prime Minister @narendramodi featuring fabricated statements that he never made regarding the protest in Delhi.”It added, “#PIBFactCheck: This is an '#AI-generated deepfake video' shared to mislead the public. Prime Minister Narendra Modi did NOT make any such statement.”The fact-check unit said the original video shared by PM Modi had been digitally altered to create a misleading version.It further shared a link to the original, unedited video posted by the PM.The fake video circulating online showed an altered audio track in which PM Modi was allegedly made to say, "We are warning people against participating in the Cockroach Janata Party protest. Those who defy this warning will face strict action from the Government of India to ensure that such behaviour is not repeated in the future. Students are advised to focus on their education, failing which they will be compelled to face serious consequences. We are issuing a clear warning to the students."The original video, posted by PM on his official social media account on Thursday, has since garnered 334 million views on Instagram. In the video, PM Modi addressed viewers as “Friends” and spoke directly into what appeared to be a phone’s front camera, held at arm’s length, with no podium, studio setup or formal backdrop.In the video, the PM said the paper leak issue had caused difficulties for lakhs of students and their parents. He said those responsible had been arrested and that steps were being taken to ensure students did not lose an academic year.The Prime Minister also said provisions for fast-track courts had been prepared and would be taken up by the Union cabinet.The fact check unit also debunked another AI-generated video that falsely showed the PM similar remarks about the cockroach janata party protests. In this manipulated clip, Modi appeared to say, “What is the problem with these cockroaches? Even if one paper gets leaked, what is the big deal? Students can simply appear for the examination again next year.” The PIB clarified that the remarks were fabricated and shared the original video, which showed the Prime Minister speaking about the monsoon and the ongoing Monsoon session of parliament.Additionally, the PIB flagged another digitally altered video of Union minister Dharmendra Pradhan that falsely portrayed him threatening protesting students. The manipulated clip appeared to show Pradhan saying that “big leaders do not resign because of these cockroaches; they crush them under their shoes and throw them into dirty drains where they belong” and warning that protesters would “soon face grave consequences”. Refuting the claims, the PIB said, “Union Minister Dharmendra Pradhan did not make any such statement.”The fact-check unit blamed Pakistani propaganda accounts for circulating the digitally altered video containing fabricated claims. The original video was posted on the occasion of Sital Sasthi and made no reference to the protests.The manipulated clip surfaced amid continuing protests led by the CJP, which has consistently demanded that Pradhan be held accountable for the alleged NEET paper leaks and has called for the education minister's resignation as one of its principal demands.In another fact check, the government flagged a separate manipulated video involving commerce minister Piyush Goyal, which falsely claimed that Goyal had made similar threatening remarks against Jantar Mantar protests.The PIB said, “Mr Goyal has made no such statement regarding the protests.”The government urged people to verify the authenticity of videos and rely on official sources before sharing them.
Article Summary: The government has debunked doctored videos circulating on social media that wrongly showed Prime Minister Narendra Modi making threatening remarks. The Press Information Bureau (PIB) fact check unit said the clips were AI-generated deepfakes. The government also flagged manipulated videos of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and commerce minister Piyush Goyal.

Article Title: 'Barbarity of Modi govt': Rahul Gandhi attacks Centre over July 20 protest crackdown
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi attacks Modi govt over 'brutality' during July 20 student protest

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Saturday criticised the PM Modi-led Centre and the Delhi police over what he called the "brutality" during the July 20 student protests in Delhi.He said that in today's India, students protesting for their rights are getting "pellets" instead of "justice".In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi shared a video of a youth who was allegedly injured after being hit by pellets fired by the Delhi Police during the protest against paper leaks."Sahil was standing with the Tricolour in his hand, merely asking for a clean, fair exam and the fruit of his hard work--the police raised a gun and badly injured him by firing pellets. This is not British tyranny; it is the barbarity of the Modi government in independent India--where innocent students demanding their rights receive pellets instead of justice," the post read.The protesters march to Parliament turned violent, leaving more than 118 police personnel injured, including senior officers such as the Special Commissioner, Joint Commissioner, Additional Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner, Additional Deputy Commissioner and Assistant Commissioner of Police.Several women police personnel were also injured. Around 60 protesters were reportedly hurt during the clashes.Meanwhile, on Friday, the Union Cabinet approved amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, to further strengthen the anti-paper leak law amid the continuing nationwide protests over the NEET-UG issue. Sources told news agency ANI the amendment Bill is likely to be introduced in Parliament on Monday, July 27.The decision came a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in a late-night video message on X, promised "stricter" action against paper leaks as protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party continued. He also announced that the Union Cabinet would take up a draft Bill.Social activist Sonam Wangchuk has also ended his 26-day hunger strike at Medanta Hospital in the presence of Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh after receiving a written assurance from the Union government on the NEET issue and broader reforms in the country's competitive examination system
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi criticises PM Modi-led Centre and Delhi police over 'brutality' during July 20 student protests in Delhi. In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi shared a video of a youth who was allegedly injured after being hit by pellets fired by the Delhi Police during the protest.

Article Title: 'Rewarding corruption': CJP attacks Centre over education secretary's replacement
Article Text:
Education secretary's transfer triggers fresh CJP attack on Centre

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday alleged that the transfer of the Education Secretary amounted to "rewarding corruption instead of ensuring accountability". He claimed that the official had been replaced by an IAS officer from the Animal Husbandry Department who faces "severe multi-crore corruption charges"."Last night, the Education Secretary was transferred. He was replaced by an IAS officer from the Animal Husbandry Department who has severe multi-crore corruption charges against him. The entire crisis around paper leaks and NEET was about systemic corruption," Dipke said in a post on X.Abhijeet further said that replacing one bureaucrat with another facing "serious corruption allegations" was "a direct insult to young people across India".Questioning whether this was the "compromise" the government expected students to accept, he asserted that "this is not accountability" and said the protest would continue until Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns."Replacing one bureaucrat with another facing serious corruption allegations is a direct INSULT to young people across India.Is this the "compromise" the government expects us to accept? This is not accountability. We will not stop until Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns," Dipke added.The Centre on Thursday carried out a major bureaucratic reshuffle, making 13 secretary-level appointments across ministries and departments, including key changes in the education ministry, amid continuing protests over the alleged NEET paper leak.Senior IAS officer Naresh Pal Gangwar has been appointed Secretary, Department of Higher Education, while T K Anil Kumar has been named Secretary, Department of School Education and Literacy. According to an order issued by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC), Gangwar, a 1994-batch IAS officer of the Rajasthan cadre, will succeed Vineet Joshi as Secretary of the Department of Higher Education.The agitation over the NEET paper leak spread across several states on Friday, a day after CJP called for nationwide demonstrations. Protesters condemned the Delhi Police crackdown on July 20 and reiterated their demand for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.As the protests gathered momentum across states, the Congress directed its state units to organise candlelight marches and 'satyagraha' in every district on Saturday evening to protest against the "irregularities in the NEET and CBSE examinations and the subsequent repressive actions by the Modi government".On Friday, a high-level meeting between leaders of CJP and senior BJP leaders, including Union Health Minister JP Nadda and Union Minister Jitendra Singh, was held at the Constitution Club in New Delhi.Earlier, activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike at Medanta Hospital in the presence Nadda and Jitendra Singh after the Union government gave a written assurance on the NEET examination issue and broader systemic reforms to the country's competitive examination framework.Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi assured that strict action would be taken against those responsible for the alleged paper leaks. He also said the Union Cabinet would consider a draft Bill proposing fast-track courts and stricter punishment for offenders.
Article Summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said the transfer amounted to "rewarding corruption instead of ensuring accountability" He claimed that the official had been replaced by an IAS officer from the Animal Husbandry Department who faces "severe multi-crore corruption charges" The Centre on Thursday carried out a major bureaucratic reshuffle.

Article Title: Gen Z outreach: PM Modi asks ministers to shore up presence on Insta
Article Text:
PM Modi on video

NEW DELHI: Buoyed by the response to his midnight post on Instagram Thursday, which got 305 million views, PM Modi Friday returned to the social media platform. "Thank you, friends. I had an opportunity to connect with you late last night. The way you responded to my video post and gave constructive suggestions, thanks to everybody. Your love will continue and our bond will strengthen," the PM said, reports Dipak Dash.His remarks reflected satisfaction, with officials calling it a "successful connect" with Gen Z, who have been wooed by CJP and other opponents. Within minutes, Friday's video had garnered 9.3 million views.This came barely hours after PM urged his Cabinet colleagues to use more of Instagram, saying it will help them stay connected with the youth. He was interacting with them after the Cabinet meeting on Friday. Official sources said PM's choice of Instagram to announce govt's decision to toughen the anti-paper leak law earned him around 1 million new followers.Prime Minister Narendra Modi asked ministers how many of them were actively using social media platforms such as Instagram.He said the platform has been popular with large sections of youth and emphasised using the social networking site to connect with them.PM Modi has been using Instagram since 2014.His advice comes amid a growing sense that BJP, which successfully leveraged mass use of WhatsApp to steal a march over its rivals, runs the risk of ceding the advantage in reaching out to Gen Z, which is not as enamoured of the messaging platform and is more comfortable with the photo & short form video service.PM Modi, a tech enthusiast, has repeatedly urged his ministers to hold interactive sessions with youth on this platform. He has said govt as well as BJP should more active on social media. Chairing the council of ministers meeting in Jan 2023, he had stressed that social media had emerged as the main source of information for large sections of the youth and its growing allure needed to be harnessed.
Article Summary: PM Modi returns to Instagram to thank his followers for their support. His midnight post on Thursday got 305 million views. PM Modi urged Cabinet colleagues to use more of Instagram. He said it will help them stay connected with the youth. His choice of Instagram to announce govt's decision to toughen the anti-paper leak law earned him around 1 million new followers.

Article Title: CJP protest: Delhi Metro shuts 17 stations for third day; see full list
Article Text:
17 Delhi Metro stations will be closed for entry and exit from Friday morning.

The stations that will remain closed are:

Lok Kalyan Marg

Rajiv Chowk

Patel Chowk

NEW DELHI: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) on Friday announced that 17 metro stations across the national capital will remain closed for entry and exit from 7.30am on Friday until further instructions, citing "security reasons".The latest advisory marks the third consecutive day of metro disruptions in central Delhi amid the ongoing Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protest at Jantar Mantar.In a post on X, the DMRC said interchange facilities will remain available at Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House and Central Secretariat despite the closures.The decision comes a day after the DMRC shut 17 stations on Thursday, following the closure of 16 stations on Wednesday, when hundreds of office-goers, students and other commuters were stranded during the morning rush hour.Entry gates at Mandi House, Rajiv Chowk and Central Secretariat were reopened later on Thursday night.The repeated closures come amid heightened security across central Delhi following the July 20 'Sansad Chalo' march, which witnessed clashes between protesters and police near Parliament.Since then, authorities have maintained heavy security deployment around Jantar Mantar, Parliament and adjoining areas, with prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) remaining in force across the New Delhi district.The CJP has continued its sit-in at Jantar Mantar, demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET paper leak and broader reforms in the examination system.The DMRC has advised commuters to plan their journeys accordingly, adding that normal operations at the affected stations will resume only after further instructions.
Article Summary: 17 Delhi Metro stations will remain closed for entry and exit from 7.30am on Friday until further instructions, citing "security reasons" The latest advisory marks the third consecutive day of metro disruptions in central Delhi amid the ongoing Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protest at Jantar Mantar.

Article Title: 3 years on, SIT probe complete in just 10% of Manipur riot cases
Article Text: NEW DELHI: More than three years after Kuki-Meitei ethnic clashes singed Manipur and claimed 260 lives, Supreme Court was informed Friday that probes into only 10% of the 3,000-odd cases had been completed by SITs of state police while CBI had investigated the majority of the 31 cases referred to it.Appearing for the CBI, additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the central probe agency had filed chargesheets in 21 cases and closure reports in six, of which three had been accepted. It was continuing investigations into the remaining four cases.Former Maharashtra DGP Dattatray Padsalgikar, who was appointed to oversee the investigations, informed the court through a report that of the 3,020 cases being probed by the SITs across eight districts, chargesheets had been filed in only 301 cases and trial had commenced in 10.The CJI-led bench told the investigators to act expeditiously. Given the volume of cases, SC mulled setting up special courts to try these exclusively. It sought responses to this from Manipur govt and the high courts of Assam and Manipur.SC had transferred investigations into cases of rape-murder other heinous offence to CBI and shifted their trial to Guwahati. The central agency told the court that examination of witnesses residing in Manipur through video-conferencing was a challenge because of law-and-order situations, non-cooperation and language barriers as they spoke different dialects.Senior advocate Ngangom Junior Luwang complained that no effort had been made to trace 30 missing people and without their remains, authorities were not issuing death certificates required for other purposes. SC asked him to approach Manipur high court.Advocate Sharukh Alam submitted that land belonging to churches vandalised during the clashes were getting encroached upon and said govt had taken no steps to reconstruct them. Bhati said govt's priority was to reconstruct damaged dwelling units. The bench said govt was right to prioritise reconstructing houses but asked it to take steps to stop encroachment of places of worship.
Article Summary: Kuki-Meitei ethnic clashes singed Manipur and claimed 260 lives. Only 10% of the 3,000-odd cases had been completed by state police. CBI had investigated the majority of the 31 cases referred to it.

Article Title: Students' stir: CJP-Centre 3rd round of talks today; PM Modi, Wangchuk release late night videos - top developments
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and activist Sonam Wangchuk. The two shared video messages on social media.

Here are the top developments:

'Your love and trust gave me strength': PM Modi shares new video

After 26 days of hunger, do I need to prove my sincerity?': Sonam Wangchuk

NTA sacks 47 officials, recruitment overhaul begins

Second round of talks ends without breakthrough

Centre seeks more time on Pradhan's resignation

Rahul Gandhi reiterates students' demands

Cabinet approves tougher anti-paper leak law

Supreme Court to hear police action pleas; CJI clarifies earlier remarks

PM Modi promises stricter action

NEW DELHI: The stand-off between the Centre and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over the alleged NEET paper leak continued on Friday, with no breakthrough on the protesters' key demand for the resignation of union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.While the government sought more time to respond after the second round of talks, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi renewed his attack on the Centre, reiterated the students' demands and accused the government of using force against peaceful protesters.Meanwhile, the National Testing Agency (NTA) has terminated the services of 47 officials as part of a major overhaul following the controversy over alleged paper leaks and examination-related irregularities. The move is part of a wider restructuring of the NTA aimed at strengthening accountability and restoring confidence in the examination system.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday shared another video message on social media, thanking people for their support as protests led by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak continued.In the video posted on Instagram, PM Modi said, "Your love and trust gave me strength," while reiterating his commitment to the welfare of students and the government's resolve to act against those responsible for examination irregularities.The latest outreach comes a day after the Prime Minister released an unusual selfie-style video beginning with the words "Hello friends", in which he acknowledged that paper leaks were "not an ordinary matter" and assured students and their families that the government would take stricter action.Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Friday shared an emotional message on social media, questioning why he still had to prove his commitment to the cause.In a post on X, Wangchuk wrote, "AFTER 26 DAYS OF HUNGER DO I NEED TO PROVE MY SINCERITY !!!"The post comes as Wangchuk ended his hunger strike, drawing attention to his demands and sparking reactions on social media.The National Testing Agency (NTA) has terminated 47 officials as part of its biggest overhaul since its formation, with some of those removed also facing legal and criminal action based on internal inquiries and inputs from investigating agencies, government sources said.The agency has also begun rebuilding its workforce by recruiting four General Managers and 16 Young Professionals through the UPSC's PRATIBHA Setu talent pool.The new appointments will focus on cybersecurity, digital forensics, test-centre operations and assessment research, and will be overseen by the K Radhakrishnan-led monitoring committee, which is scheduled to hold its first meeting on July 25.The restructuring follows the alleged NEET-UG paper leak and includes plans to reduce dependence on contractual and outsourced staff, strengthen examination security, review outsourcing practices, and prepare for the shift to computer-based NEET-UG examinations from 2027.Officials said further action and reforms are expected as investigations into examination-related irregularities continue.A CJP delegation held a nearly two-hour meeting with Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh at the Constitution Club in New Delhi. The delegation submitted three key demands and a five-point reform charter, but the meeting ended without a final decision.Addressing reporters, Nadda said the government would respond after internal consultations."The meeting went on for almost two hours. They had three main demands and five reform suggestions for exams. We have told them that we will meet them again tomorrow afternoon and tell them about the discussion we had within the government," he said.The next round of talks has been scheduled for Saturday afternoon.CJP leaders said the Centre had sought time till Saturday afternoon to respond to their demand for Pradhan's resignation, which they described as non-negotiable.CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said the government had expressed in-principle approval to the other two demands."The government has asked for time till tomorrow afternoon on our demand for Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. We hope the government will remove him soon," he said.CJP leader Saurav Das said the delegation had also sought Rs 1 crore compensation for the families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide, withdrawal of FIRs and legal cases against protesting students, and a written sovereign guarantee that similar action would not be taken against peaceful protesters in the future. According to the delegation, the government accepted the compensation and FIR-related demands in principle.Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi renewed his demand for Dharmendra Pradhan's removal, alleging that the education minister was responsible for the crisis."Dharmendra Pradhan is a criminal education minister. He has to be removed. He is a symbol of the collapse of our education system. He has to go," Gandhi said.He said students were demanding the removal of the education minister, action against those responsible for the alleged pellet gun use and lathi-charge during the protests, and an apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi.During the press conference, Rahul also presented a protester whom he alleged had suffered pellet gun injuries during the Jantar Mantar protest."His eye has suffered damage, and he has lost his vision," Gandhi said, while alleging that the government had falsely denied using pellet guns against protesters.The government has denied using pellet guns during the protest.The union cabinet approved amendments to the Prevention of Paper Leak law, proposing stricter punishment for those involved in examination paper leaks.According to sources, the proposed amendments provide for a maximum jail term of 10 years, a fine of up to Rs 10 crore and an increase in the minimum imprisonment from three years to five years.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the government would introduce the Bill in Parliament soon and that Prime Minister Narendra Modi had directed that there should be no delay. Rijiju also criticised the Opposition for disrupting Parliament and urged members to allow a discussion on the issue.The Supreme Court on Friday agreed to hear on July 27 two petitions alleging excessive police action against students protesting over the alleged NEET paper leak.Earlier in the day, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant clarified that reports claiming he had refused to hear a petition on the issue were incorrect."In the last two days, a completely false statement was made that a matter was filed," the CJI said, adding that only a representation had been submitted at that stage and describing the reports as "irresponsible and reckless".A day before the Cabinet decision, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that the government would introduce legislation providing for fast-track courts and stricter punishment in paper leak cases."Paper leaks are not an ordinary matter. For lakhs of students and their parents, it is extremely painful," Modi said.The Prime Minister said the government had ensured that nearly 22 lakh students did not lose an academic year by conducting the examinations again. He also welcomed activist Sonam Wangchuk's decision to end his 26-day hunger strike, while the CJP maintained that its protest would continue until Dharmendra Pradhan resigns.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and activist Sonam Wangchuk share video messages on social media. Stand-off between Centre and Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over alleged NEET paper leak continues. CJP delegation held nearly two-hour meeting with Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh at the Constitution Club in New Delhi.

Article Title: 'Thank you, friends': PM Modi hails 'love, support' of youth in new Insta video
Article Text:
Thank you, friends': PM Modi hails 'love, support' of youth in new Insta video

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday thanked young people for watching his video on examination reforms and sharing their suggestions.In a video message shared on Instagram, PM Modi expressed appreciation for the response to his address and the feedback received from students and young people."Thank you friends. I had the opportunity to meet you late last night. I appreciate the way you responded to my video and your positive suggestions. Thanks to everyone..." PM Modi said."Last night, I got the opportunity to interact with you. The way you responded to the video I posted and shared your positive suggestions—thanks to everybody. Your love and support continue, and that our connection grows even stronger and more active," he further said.The caption of the video read: "Thanks to the youngsters who watched my video yesterday and sent insightful suggestions."PM Modi's message comes a day after he announced that the government would introduce stricter measures to tackle examination paper leaks amid nationwide protests over alleged irregularities in the NEET-UG examination.In a video message on Thursday, PM Modi said the Union Cabinet would consider a draft Bill providing for fast-track courts and stringent punishment for those involved in paper leak cases, with efforts to pass the legislation in Parliament during the coming week."I know that paper leak is not an ordinary issue. It is very painful for lakhs of students and their guardians," the Prime Minister had said, adding that the government had already arrested those responsible and ensured that nearly 22 lakh students were able to retake the examination without losing an academic year.He had also said the proposed legislation would include provisions for fast-track courts and tougher penalties to strengthen the integrity of the country's examination system.The announcement came amid widespread protests over the alleged NEET-UG paper leak. Earlier this week, PM Modi also told the NDA Parliamentary Party that the government was working to make the country's examination system "foolproof".
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi thanks young people for watching his video on examination reforms. PM Modi's message comes a day after he announced stricter measures to tackle paper leaks. Announcement came amid nationwide protests over alleged irregularities in the NEET-UG examination. In a video message shared on Instagram, PM Modi expressed appreciation for the response.

Article Title: Grain, not guns: MEA rejects Russia's claim on deadly ship attack that killed 4 Indians
Article Text:
India reiterates concerns to Russia

Shipping attacks under scrutiny

NEW DELHI: Ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday said the merchant vessel MV Golden Leo, which was struck in a Russian attack off Ukraine's Odesa port earlier this week, was carrying grain and not military cargo, effectively rejecting Moscow's assertion that the ship was transporting weapons for Ukraine.Responding to questions on the Russian claim, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the information available with the Indian government showed the Guinea-Bissau-flagged vessel had loaded grain before leaving Odesa."As per information made available to us from the Directorate General of Maritime Administration, India, MV Golden Leo, the Guinea-Bissau-flagged commercial vessel involved in the tragic incident in the Odesa port, had loaded grain as cargo prior to its departure on July 19," Jaiswal said at the ministry's weekly media briefing."We once again reiterate that commercial shipping and seafarers must not be targeted under any circumstances," he added.The clarification came days after a Russian strike on the merchant vessel killed 10 people, including four Indian seafarers, marking the first deaths of Indian sailors since the Russia-Ukraine war began.Jaiswal said external affairs minister S Jaishankar reiterated India's position during his meeting with Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov in Manila on Wednesday.India had also summoned Russian Charge d'Affaires Vladimir Ladanov on Tuesday to convey its "grave concerns" and "unequivocal condemnation" of the attack on the commercial vessel.The move followed remarks by Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov, who defended Russia's actions, saying Moscow would continue targeting vessels carrying arms for Ukraine.Peskov said Russian forces would continue striking ships involved in transporting "ammunition, weapons, and so on" for the Kyiv government.India's latest statement, citing cargo details provided by the directorate general of maritime administration, contradicts that assertion.MV Golden Leo, carrying 17 crew members including five Indians, was hit by Russian cruise missiles while leaving the Ukrainian port of Odesa.The attack has intensified India's concerns over the safety of commercial shipping in the conflict zone.Separately, the MEA also condemned another attack on the commercial vessel MV OMORFI in the Black Sea that killed an Indian national, calling attacks on commercial shipping "unacceptable" and urging all parties to ensure the safety of maritime navigation and the uninterrupted flow of global trade.With two fatal incidents involving Indian seafarers in less than a week, India has repeatedly stressed that civilian merchant vessels and their crews must not be targeted during the ongoing conflict.
Article Summary: MV Golden Leo, carrying 17 crew members including five Indians, was hit by Russian cruise missiles while leaving the Ukrainian port of Odesa. The move followed remarks by Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov, who defended Russia's actions, saying Moscow would continue targeting vessels carrying arms for Ukraine.

Article Title: SC agrees to hear PIL against police excesses on Monday
Article Text:
SC to hear PIL

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Friday agreed to hear Monday a PIL by an advocate for framing and scrupulous implementation of national guidelines ensuring "no police officer or security personnel shall carry out crowd control, public assembly management or arrests in plainclothes without displaying identity".CJI Surya Kant clarified that he was misquoted in the media when he refused to entertain another advocate who was highlighting the issues arising from the July 20 protest march and police action.In his plea, Shailendra Mani Tripathi sought an independent commission headed by a retired SC judge to inquire into the excessive force used against students and arbitrary detentions by Delhi Police during Monday's CJP's march to Parliament, and suspension and prosecution of all identified delinquent police officers.He urged SC to ban “rolling, repetitive, or blanket prohibitory orders in any area without an objectively verified, proximate and recorded threat of grave public disorder”.He also said the court must direct authorities not to prosecute any person for political dissent, academic critique, peaceful protest or criticism of govt unless there is a “direct, proximate, and imminent incitement to armed rebellion or secessionist violence”.The PIL, filed through advocate Chand Qureshi, sought a declaration that “any use of coercive force by unidentifiable or plainclothes personnel during public assemblies as arbitrary, illegal and a major service misconduct”.Referring to the earlier petition and his reported remarks, the CJI said, “He (petitioner) said he has filed a petition and sent a letter to SC. On inquiry, we found that neither the petition had been filed nor the letter had been sent. How can a court entertain a plea without a single paper before it?” the CJI asked.
Article Summary: CJI Surya Kant clarified that he was misquoted in the media when he refused to entertain another advocate. Shailendra Mani Tripathi sought an independent commission headed by a retired SC judge to inquire into the excessive force used against students and arbitrary detentions.

Article Title: 'Have a heart': Sonam Wangchuk's wife slams critics after he ends 26-day hunger strike
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Gitanjali Angmo on Friday came to the defence of her husband Sonam Wangchuk 's decision to end his 26-day hunger strike against the NEET paper leak, urging critics to show compassion instead of rushing to judge him.In a post on X, Angmo said Wangchuk had "chosen sacrifice over comfort" and added that not everyone was qualified to judge a life dedicated to selfless service."Before you rush to criticise Sonam Wangchuk, first pause to earn the ethos of fasting for 26 days for a cause larger than yourself," Angmo said."He lies in the ICU today, having lost 11 kg, including muscle mass, because he chose sacrifice over comfort. The least we can offer him is a day of compassion before burdening him with our own expectations and political calculations. Not everyone is qualified to judge a life of selfless service. One must first earn the moral stature to do so. Please. Have a heart," she added.This comes after Wangchuk ended his hunger strike in the presence of Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, saying the decision followed prolonged negotiations and was taken to avoid any possibility of violence in the country.In a separate post on X, Wangchuk said he broke his fast in the presence of the two Union ministers and senior leaders of the Apex Body of Leh Ladakh.He added that 65 MPs from different political parties had either visited him or signed letters urging him to end the fast.Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) said it would continue its nationwide "peaceful protests" demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak."The Cockroach Janata Party's peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar will continue until Dharmendra Pradhan resigns," CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said in a statement after Wangchuk ended his hunger strike.
Article Summary: Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike against the NEET paper leak. His wife Gitanjali Angmo urged critics to show compassion instead of rushing to judge him. Wangchuk said he broke his fast in the presence of two Union ministers and senior leaders.

Article Title: Police identify 2,500 people with criminal records at Jantar Mantar protest through facial recognition cameras
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Delhi police has identified more than 2,500 people with criminal backgrounds through Facial Recognition System deployed around the protest site at Jantar Mantar, news agency PTI reported, citing sources."The technology has so far helped identify over 2,500 persons with criminal antecedents. It acts as a strong deterrent and allows us to keep a close watch on those who may attempt to misuse the protest to create law and order problems," sources told PTI.According to the sources, the FRS units have been positioned at key entry and exit points around the protest site and are directly linked to the Delhi Police database."The objective is to ensure that people with criminal backgrounds do not exploit the protest to create law and order issues," sources told PTI."The system is connected with the Delhi Police database and can identify wanted criminals, absconders, history-sheeters, and Bad Characters (BCs) whose details already exist in police records," they added.According to an officer, the FRS does not target ordinary protesters but is meant to identify those with criminal antecedents who may attempt to take advantage of large gatherings."These are high-resolution cameras capable of capturing facial images even from a distance.Once a face is captured, it is quickly matched with the police database. If a wanted or absconding accused is detected, the concerned police unit is immediately alerted, and legal action can be initiated without delay," he said.Police said the technology will also help identify habitual offenders who have repeatedly figured in criminal cases and are listed as "Bad Characters" in Delhi Police records."The deployment acts as both a preventive and investigative tool. It helps us remain alert against anti-social elements who may try to infiltrate the protest, create a nuisance, or disturb law and order," another officer said.The installation of the FRS forms part of enhanced security arrangements around Jantar Mantar.
Article Summary: Delhi police has identified more than 2,500 people with criminal backgrounds through Facial Recognition System deployed around Jantar Mantar. FRS units have been positioned at key entry and exit points around the protest site and are directly linked to the Delhi Police database.

Article Title: Treat digital arrests and cyber frauds as organised crime: SC
Article Text:
‘Invoke Stringent Laws To Curb Such Crimes’

NEW DELHI: Maintaining its zero-tolerance approach towards digital arrest and cyber fraud cases, SC Friday said police must invoke charges under stringent laws to prevent such organised crimes.Rejecting the bail plea of Mohamad, aka MD, accused in a case relating to digital arrest followed by fraudsters posing as policemen and showing forged SC orders to coerce a man to part with Rs 76 lakh last year, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, "Digital arrest and cyber fraud cases must be equated with robbery and dacoity. Why are these offences not classified as organised crime?" It asked Gujarat police why they had not added charges under Gujarat Control of Terrorism and Organised Crime Act, which came into force in 2019.When the petitioner's counsel Aastha Mehta said the accused had been in custody for more than a year, and he be granted bail as investigation in the case had been completed, the bench said, "If you want the court to entertain the plea, then the first thing we will do is to add graver charges under the law on organised crime."It was alleged that unknown persons impersonating Mumbai policemen accused the complainant of being involved in a money laundering case and placed him under digital arrest for two days through continuous video calls, during which they forwarded him forged documents purporting to be arrest warrants and judicial orders issued by SC through WhatsApp.SC had taken cognisance of rising digital arrest scams, mostly targeting senior citizens, and asked CBI to probe cases pan-India, and was instrumental in activating an inter-departmental mechanism involving different agencies to implement steps to curb this menace.
Article Summary: SC rejects bail plea of Mohamad, aka MD, accused in a case relating to digital arrest. Fraudsters posing as policemen used forged SC orders to coerce a man to part with Rs 76 lakh. It was alleged that unknown persons impersonating Mumbai policemen accused the complainant of being involved in a money laundering case.

Article Title: Dharmendra Pradhan must go to let Parl function: Oppn

The anti-BJP parties will meet Monday morning to take a final stand on the issue, but a flurry of statements from opposition netas suggested they are unlikely to relent. With CJP in talks with govt, there was some anxiety in the opposition camp about the stand it might take. Article Title: Amid manhunt for J&K cop’s terrorist killers, detentions spike to 3.5k
Article Text:
Detentions across J&K linked to the terrorist killing of head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi rose to 3,500

SRINAGAR: Detentions across J&K linked to the terrorist killing of head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi rose to 3,500 Friday as police stepped up their crackdown on suspected sympathisers of armed groups.A senior police officer said around 700 people were detained for interrogation in Srinagar alone since the terror attack last Wednesday, in which Qureshi, who was on Amarnath Yatra duty at Lal Chowk in Anantnag, was killed. “Due process has been followed in all detentions,” he said.DGP Nalin Prabhat convened a meeting for a comprehensive security review in Srinagar, with participating officers presenting their assessments of the prevailing security scenario across the Union territory.“The meeting focused on the current operational environment, threat perception and preparedness of field formations,” a police spokesperson said. “The DGP directed the officers to intensify area domination and night domination, particularly in vulnerable urban areas.”Home minister Amit Shah had a phone conversation with the slain head constable’s son after J&K leader of the opposition Sunil Sharma visited the family at their residence in Lalpora Beerwah of Budgam.Lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha, too, made a trip earlier and assured the bereaved family of the administration’s support.CM Omar Abdullah was critical of the detentions and Thursday’s controlled explosions targeting the family homes of two wanted Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists. “I understand the police’s anger. But there is a Supreme Court order that such summary action should not be taken,” he said.Recalling his first stint as CM when J&K was a state, Omar said he knew “at the time that this problem (terrorism) cannot be resolved without the people’s support”.He said the backlash against terrorist outfits after last year’s attack on tourists in Pahalgam showed that ordinary people do not support them. “Even today, people are angry that a police head constable has been killed so brutally. But when the number of arrests rises from hundreds to 2,000 or 2,500, that public anger risks being redirected against us,” he said. “I hope we take our people along with us in this fight.”Ex-CM and PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti said detaining thousands and demolishing the family homes of two “alleged” terrorists “amounts to collective punishment that has no place in a democracy”. People’s Conference chairperson Sajad Lone warned that the police’s response to one of their own being killed by terrorists would “do more harm”.
Article Summary: Detentions across J&K linked to the terrorist killing of head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi rose to 3,500 Friday. Police stepped up their crackdown on suspected sympathisers of armed groups. A senior police officer said around 700 people were detained for interrogation in Srinagar alone since the terror attack.

Article Title: Amid rain & fresh landslides, Jammu-Srinagar NH closure enters Day 3
Article Text:
Torrential rain triggered fresh landslides across J&K

JAMMU: Torrential rain triggered fresh landslides across J&K on Friday, prompting authorities to keep Jammu-Srinagar National Highway (NH-44) closed for traffic on the third consecutive day. The suspension of all major pilgrimages in the Union Territory — Amarnath, Vaishno Devi, Machhail Mata, Shiv Khori and Sarthal Mata Yatras — in place since July 19, continued for the sixth day.Officials said the NH was blocked at Deohal bridge, Samroli and Jakhani in Udhampur district, and Banihal in Ramban district. More than 1,000 vehicles remained stranded at Ramban, Nagrota, Jammu, Udhampur, Lakhanpur and Samba due to the closure. Amid concerns of fresh landslides and shooting stones along the stretch, officials urged commuters not to travel on the road until it was declared safe for movement.Kishtwar district magistrate, in an order issued Friday, barred all movement along the Kishtwar-Paddar-Gulabgarh axis from July 25-27 — in view of rain-triggered safety hazards along the stretch, such as slippery road conditions, landslips and persistent shooting stones — until further notice.All ceremonial and customary religious rituals associated with the Machhail Mata Yatra shall be performed symbolically, the order stated, advising pilgrims and the public against venturing towards Gulabgarh or Machhail between July 25-27.Rain-triggered flash floods struck Barkuanda area in Bupp, Udhampur, early Friday, affecting several households. There were no casualties. Damage assessment was underway, officials said.
Article Summary: Torrential rain triggered fresh landslides across J&K on Friday, prompting authorities to keep Jammu-Srinagar National Highway (NH-44) closed for traffic. More than 1,000 vehicles remained stranded at Ramban, Nagrota, Jammu, Udhampur, Lakhanpur and Samba due to the closure.

Article Title: 'Position remains unchanged': India rejects Pakistan's Asean remarks, reiterates stand on Indus Waters Treaty
Article Text:
'Position remains unchanged': India rejects Pakistan's Asean remarks, reiterates stand on Indus Waters Treaty

NEW DELHI: External affairs ministry on Friday strongly rejected Pakistan's remarks at the Asean Regional Forum and reiterated that India's position on the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) remains unchanged, saying the treaty will remain in abeyance until Pakistan 'irrevocably and credibly' ends its support for cross-border terrorism.The MEA also dismissed Pakistan's allegations that India had deliberately caused flooding in Pakistan, calling the claims 'baseless' and attributing the rise in the Chenab river's water level to heavy monsoon rainfall.Addressing a weekly media briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Pakistan had used the Asean forum to raise issues that India had already rejected."On the ASEAN forum, Pakistan utilised it to make certain remarks. On that, we have made categorical rejections of the issues raised through our press release. You would have seen our statement. On the Indus Waters Treaty, our position remains unchanged and very clear. The Indus Waters Treaty remains in abeyance until Pakistan irrevocably and credibly abjures its support for cross-border terrorism," Jaiswal said.The remarks came a day after India categorically rejected Pakistan's comments at the Asean Regional Forum in Manila, accusing Islamabad of using the multilateral platform to spread 'state-sponsored disinformation' and divert attention from its record of sponsoring cross-border terrorism.Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and foreign minister Ishaq Dar, who represented Islamabad at the forum, raised the Jammu and Kashmir issue and criticised India's decision to keep the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance.India responded by stating that Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh 'have been, are and will always remain integral and inalienable parts of India' and that Pakistan had no locus standi to comment on the matter.Responding to another question during the briefing, Jaiswal rejected Pakistani media reports alleging that India had deliberately caused flooding in Pakistan by manipulating river flows."We have seen Pakistani media reports alleging that India is deliberately causing flooding in Pakistan and such allegations are baseless and contrary to the facts," he said.Jaiswal said the recent increase in the Chenab river's flow was caused by intense monsoon rainfall over Jammu and adjoining catchment areas between July 20 and 23.He observed that Pakistan's own Flood Forecasting Division in Lahore had, in its advisory issued on July 22, attributed the high flood levels in the Chenab to heavy rainfall over the upper catchment and had forecast that the high flows would gradually recede as rainfall decreased."The rise in river flows is, therefore, a natural hydrological response to heavy monsoon rainfall and not the result of any deliberate action by India. Attempts to portray a weather-driven flood event as an upstream intervention are factually incorrect, technically untenable, and contradicted by Pakistan's own official flood advisories," Jaiswal said.He also rejected allegations that India had failed to issue flood warnings, saying river flows during the period did not reach levels requiring special alerts."Any suggestion that India deliberately withheld flood-related information is, therefore, without factual basis. Nevertheless, like last year, India will share high-flood data with Pakistan on humanitarian grounds, through diplomatic channels as and when a situation arises," he added.External affairs minister S Jaishankar attended the Asean-India, East Asia Summit and Asean Regional Forum ministerial meetings in Manila over the last two days.
Article Summary: India rejects Pakistan's Asean remarks, reiterates stand on Indus Waters Treaty. India says treaty will remain in abeyance until Pakistan 'irrevocably and credibly' ends its support for cross-border terrorism. MEA also dismissed Pakistan's allegations that India had deliberately caused flooding in Pakistan.

Article Title: CJP students protest: RAF probes excessive force, pellet gun charges in July 20 crackdown
Article Text:
The violence erupted during CJP-led 'Chalo Sansad' march on July 20. (ANI photo)

NEW DELHI: The Rapid Action Force (RAF) has begun an internal verification of the conduct of its personnel during the July 20 student protests in Delhi, amid allegations of excessive use of force and the use of pellet guns to disperse demonstrators, officials told news agency PTI on Friday.The Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), under which the RAF functions, has directed the inspector general of the anti-riot unit to verify the sequence of events involving its teams during the protest, including the actions taken to control demonstrators and instances where RAF personnel themselves came under attack, officials said.A formal Court of Inquiry has not yet been ordered. According to CRPF officials, such a probe will be initiated only if the ongoing verification establishes grounds for further investigation.The violence erupted during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led 'Chalo Sansad' march on July 20. Students had marched from Jantar Mantar towards Parliament, demanding Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over the alleged NEET question paper leak. The protest ended in clashes with security personnel, who used batons and tear gas to disperse the crowd.Officials told PTI that the RAF has taken cognisance of multiple videos and photographs circulating on social media showing personnel in the force's distinctive blue camouflage uniforms using lathis and firearms during the operation.The footage also includes visuals of RAF personnel allegedly being surrounded and attacked by protesters."All legal procedures stipulated to examine the conduct of personnel during such operational duties will be followed," a senior officer told PTI.Officials said the RAF is equipped with 12-bore pump-action guns, commonly referred to as pellet guns, as part of its standard riot-control equipment. Under the force's standard operating procedure (SOP), these weapons may be used only in extreme situations where personnel face a serious threat to their lives.The SOP also requires the weapons to be fitted with a deflector so that the metal or rubber pellets cause limited injuries and are aimed only below the waist, officials said.The verification assumes significance amid allegations that at least two students sustained pellet injuries during the July 20 clashes and were admitted to hospitals.While the Delhi Police has denied possessing pellet guns and termed reports suggesting their use as misleading, neither the CRPF nor the RAF has publicly confirmed or denied whether RAF personnel fired pellet ammunition during the protest.Apart from the allegations of excessive force, the verification will also examine videos showing RAF personnel allegedly being attacked by protesters, footage of an RAF uniformed man appearing to trip a running protester, and another clip that purportedly shows a stun gun being used during the clashes, officials said.The CRPF has also instructed commanders of RAF and other units deployed during the protests not to speak to the media after comments made earlier this week by a woman RAF officer were considered "undesirable", officials said.Separately, the force is examining social media posts allegedly made by RAF assistant commandant Sonia Sehrawat through her Instagram account to determine whether they violated the CRPF's social media policy, according to officials. The paramilitary force's 2023 guidelines prohibit personnel from commenting on controversial or politically sensitive issues online.
Article Summary: The Rapid Action Force (RAF) has begun an internal verification of the conduct of its personnel during the July 20 student protests in Delhi. The verification comes amid allegations of excessive use of force and the use of pellet guns to disperse demonstrators. The violence erupted during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led 'Chalo Sansad' march.

Article Title: 'You do whatever you like?' Delhi HC pulls up EC for deploying school teachers for BLO duties during SIR
Article Text:
Delhi HC pulls up EC for deploying school teachers for BLO duties during SIR

NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Friday questioned the Election Commission (EC) over deploying school teachers as Booth Level Officers (BLOs) for the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in the national capital, asking under what legal authority teachers were being compelled to carry out election work.Hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) challenging the deployment of government, municipal and government-aided school teachers for BLO and SIR duties, a division bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia sought an explanation from the poll body on the legal basis for its decision.During the hearing, the bench expressed reservations over the commission's reliance on Article 324 of the Constitution."Taking shade of Article 324, you do whatever you like?" ANI quoted the chief justice saying.The court also questioned the Commission's claim that teachers were serving as "volunteers", pointing out that those refusing election duties could face disciplinary action."Make a statement that this is voluntary, and we will dispose of the petition," the Bench told the Commission.Appearing for the ECI, advocate Sanjay Vashishtha argued that the Special Intensive Revision exercise in Delhi was nearing completion and that only around 10 to 14 per cent of school teachers were eventually engaged for electoral roll revision work.He submitted that the commission derives its power to requisition staff from Section 13B(2) of the Representation of the People Act and that such powers are exercised sparingly. Vashishtha also said teachers are assigned BLO duties only during holidays and non-teaching hours in line with the commission's guidelines.The bench, however, questioned why teachers should have to give up their holidays for election work."Somebody is not interested in your honorarium or compensation. Can these instructions issued by you be said to be mandatory? Can you say no, no, no, we are compensating, please come. Destroy their holidays? Don't they need rest?" the court asked.The hearing comes days after the Office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), Delhi, issued a circular on July 23 directing district election authorities to ensure that teachers' academic responsibilities are not affected during the SIR exercise.
Article Summary: Delhi high court questions the Election Commission (EC) over deploying school teachers as Booth Level Officers (BLOs) for the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in the national capital. Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia sought an explanation from the poll body.

Article Title: Himachal Pradesh: At least 13 feared dead after taxi crushed by boulders in Lahaul-Spiti
Article Text:
Himachal Pradesh: At least 13 feared dead after taxi crushed by boulders in Lahaul-Spiti

NEW DELHI: At least 13 people, including a six-month-old infant, are feared dead after a taxi was hit by boulders on the Sansari–Killar–Tandi (SKTT) road near Kadu Nala in Himachal Pradesh's tribal Lahaul-Spiti district on Friday.The taxi, carrying 15 passengers from Udaipur in Lahaul Spiti to Pangi, was crushed when a large section of the hillside collapsed near Kadu Nala on the Udaipur-Killar stretch of the SKTT road.The route had been reopened earlier in the day after remaining closed due to a landslide, and the passengers, who had been stranded overnight in Tindi, had resumed their journey when the fresh slide struck.Police, local administration and rescue teams rushed to the spot and launched a rescue operation. One injured passenger was initially pulled out of the debris and shifted to hospital, while heavy machinery was deployed to clear the landslide and search for the remaining occupants.In a statement, Bharmour MLA Janak Raj said that 13 of the 15 occupants had lost their lives, including a six-month-old infant, while two people were safe. He said he was in constant touch with senior officials of the Chamba and Lahaul-Spiti district administrations to monitor the rescue and relief operations and ensure all possible assistance to the affected families.Expressing grief over the tragedy, the MLA conveyed his condolences to the bereaved families.Meanwhile, a woman from Kullu was killed and seven members of her family were injured after a boulder fell from a hillside while they were travelling to the Simsa temple in Mandi district on Friday morning.The accident occurred around 10 am near Gumma in Jogindernagar subdivision when the family, travelling in two vehicles from Sultanpur in Kullu district, stopped by the roadside to drink water. Moments later, a rock suddenly dislodged from the hillside and struck the group.The deceased was identified as Rameshwari Sharma, wife of Gopal Krishna and a resident of Sultanpur, Kullu. She died on the spot.
Article Summary: Taxi carrying 15 passengers from Udaipur in Lahaul Spiti to Pangi was crushed. Route had been reopened earlier in the day after remaining closed due to a landslide. Woman from Kullu was killed and seven members of her family were injured after a boulder fell from a hillside.

Article Title: 'Don't insult students' intelligence': Rahul Gandhi slams PM Modi's midnight video on paper leaks

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi early Friday attacked Prime Minister Narendra Modi accusing him of sidestepping the demand for Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan 's resignation over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak.Reacting to the Prime Minister's late-night video message on the issue, Rahul said PM Modi should not "insult the intelligence" of students and demanded Pradhan be sacked saying the PM's address failed to raise students' key concerns.In a post on X, Rahul wrote, "Mr Modi, our students are demanding Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. Don't insult their intelligence with this pathetic midnight video."Listing his demands, he said:"1. Sack Pradhan.2. Punish those who beat students.3. Apologise."The leader of oppostion's remarks came hours after Prime Minister Modi announced that the government would bring a Bill in Parliament next week providing for stringent punishment against those involved in examination paper leaks.In a self-recorded video shared on X late Thursday night, the Prime Minister said the proposed legislation, which includes provisions for Fast-Track Courts and stricter penalties, would be discussed by the Union Cabinet on Friday before being introduced in Parliament when the second week of the Monsoon Session begins on Monday."Friends, I know that paper leaks are not an ordinary matter. For lakhs of students and their parents, it is extremely painful," PM Modi said."Our most important responsibility was to ensure that a whole year for the students is not wasted. It was very important to conduct the exams immediately. The government used its full strength to arrange exams for nearly 22 lakh students in the shortest possible time. And just five or six days ago, on the 19th, the results were also announced," he said.The Prime Minister said the government was now moving towards stronger legal action."Today I have issued directions to the departments to set up Fast-Track Courts. The departments worked tirelessly and, late last night, provided me with a draft. This draft, which includes provisions for Fast-Track Courts and stringent punishments, will be discussed in the Cabinet tomorrow," he said.He added that after incorporating suggestions from Cabinet colleagues, the Bill would be finalised and introduced in Parliament next week."Nothing is more important than the welfare and future of our youth. Those who try to harm the future of our youth will not be spared," PM Modi said.The opposition has been demanding Pradhan's resignation and a detailed discussion on the alleged NEET-UG paper leak during the Monsoon Session, with the issue triggering protests both inside Parliament and on the streets.Activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike on Friday at Medanta Hospital in the presence of Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh, along with senior leaders of the Apex Body of Leh.In a post on X, Wangchuk said he decided to end the fast after prolonged discussions and in view of the possibility of violence."Just now in the presence of Union Ministers JP Nadda & Dr. Jitendra Singh and the senior leaders of Apex Body of Leh Ladakh I finally broke my fast after 26 days... This was done after a long negotiation on various conditions and in view of possible violence in the country," he said."I will explain the conditions in detail in a separate video very soon. Meanwhile urge you all to stay very vigilant about not allowing violence of any kind anywhere," he added.Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) has called for nationwide peaceful protests on Friday, reiterating its demand for Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over the alleged examination irregularities.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi accuses PM Modi of sidestepping the demand for education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak. Article Title: 'Trademark arrogance': Sonia Gandhi says Modi govt treated NEET protesters as 'enemies of nation'
Article Text:
Sonia Gandhi alleged that even students heading home were not spared as police used batons indiscriminately.

Sonia alleges 'utter impunity'

PM Modi vows stricter law

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be the priority in addressing education-related concerns? Education reforms Stronger accountability 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi on Friday launched a sharp attack on the Narendra Modi government, accusing it of responding to students' demands for accountability and education reforms with "cowardice and wanton cruelty" instead of meaningful action.She described July 20, 2026, as "a day of infamy", alleging that the Delhi Police and Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) used lathis and tear gas to disperse peaceful demonstrators. She also claimed that many protesters were injured and that even students returning home were allegedly beaten.Sonia Gandhi alleged that numerous peaceful protesters were injured, and even students heading home were not spared, as police used batons indiscriminately."The nation has seen some of the most depressing visuals of youth whose bodies have been scarred by pellets, the use of which would undoubtedly have been approved by Union home minister Amit Shah himself," the ex-Congress chief wrote in an article titled 'An education system's collapse, young India's trauma', published in The Hindu.Gandhi said the government's handling of the ongoing student protests reflected its unwillingness to engage with the concerns of young people."The videos from that day are seared into our memories and have stirred our collective conscience. Only the government and its captive media are spinning stories around this spontaneous rising tide of protest. It is time to say loud and clear: Stop, these are our sons and daughters, our young men and women," Gandhi said.She said students across the country had been demanding accountability over examination paper leaks and broader reforms in the education system, but alleged that the Centre had chosen repression over dialogue."The student protests are a natural consequence of these interrelated forces: today's bleak education landscape, which evokes only hopelessness, and the Modi government's trademark arrogance and unwillingness to be accountable or constructive," Gandhi wrote.She further alleged that the government had weakened India's education system while acting with "utter impunity, supreme self-delusion, and abject insensitivity".According to Gandhi, it was the moral, political and constitutional responsibility of every public representative to stand with students and protect their future.Referring to the police action against protesters, she claimed the use of force was consistent with the government's previous response to public demonstrations."We all remember vividly how armed policemen and paramilitary forces ravaged university campuses during the Citizenship (Amendment) Act-National Register of Citizens protests in 2020. The unacceptable excesses against India's women wrestlers can never be erased from our memories," she said.Gandhi also criticised the police action during the recent protests over the alleged NEET paper leak and the state of the education system."Their demands have been straightforward and to the point: accountability from the Government of India and education reform. The Narendra Modi government has responded to their courage with cowardice and wanton cruelty, treating them not as inheritors of the future but as enemies of the nation," she said.Sonia's remarks came a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that the Union Cabinet would discuss a Bill to strengthen the existing anti-cheating law with stricter penalties for those involved in examination paper leaks.In a recorded message released late on Thursday night, the Prime Minister said the proposed legislation would include provisions for fast-track courts and tougher punishment for offenders. He said the Bill would be finalised after Cabinet approval and introduced in Parliament when the second week of the Monsoon Session begins.Modi said the government had been working for the past two and a half months to address concerns arising from the alleged NEET paper leak. He added that the Centre had ensured that nearly 22 lakh students did not lose an academic year by conducting the re-examination and declaring the results.The Prime Minister's announcement came shortly after the government replaced the Education Secretary amid the continuing protests over the alleged paper leak.Amid ongoing protests, the government named animal husbandry secretary Naresh Pal Gangwar the new secretary for higher education, while TK Anil Kumar the new school education secretary. Incumbent Vineet Joshi, who had charge of both, moved to low-profile panchayati raj department.Officials said the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) had remained in close touch with the education ministry over issues related to the NEET re-test and the implementation of recommendations made by the K Radhakrishnan Committee on reforms to the National Testing Agency (NTA).
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi alleges that even students heading home were not spared as police used batons indiscriminately. She described July 20, 2026, as "a day of infamy", alleging that the Delhi Police and Central Armed Police Forces used lathis and tear gas to disperse peaceful demonstrators.

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Friday expressed relief after activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike, while making it clear that its peaceful agitation at Delhi's Jantar Mantar would continue until Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns.In a post on X, Dipke thanked Wangchuk for what he described as an "extraordinary courage and sacrifice" during the fast.Dipke wrote.However, he further said the end of Wangchuk's fast would not mark the end of the movement.Dipke said.Wangchuk had been on an indefinite hunger strike over alleged irregularities in the NEET examination and the government's handling of the issue.Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his indefinite hunger strike shortly after midnight at Medanta Hospital in Gurugram in the presence of Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh.He said the decision followed prolonged negotiations with the government and was taken "in view of possible violence in the country.""Just now in the presence of Union Ministers JP Nadda & Dr Jitendra Singh and the senior leaders of Apex Body of Leh Ladakh I finally broke my fast after 26 days.
