Article Title: Low-key Nadda emerges as govt point man in talks with protesters
Article Text:
Nadda emerges as key negotiator from govt's side

NEW DELHI: As the govt's main interlocutor with students protesting under the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) banner, Union health minister JP Nadda has been thrust into the limelight, holding talks with them and visiting the injured in hospitals.This is an interesting turn in Nadda's journey. The former BJP president is not really known for revelling in the spotlight and is more at ease in closed-door political meetings than being in the middle of public attention. That his comments rarely stoke any controversy or ruffle others is being considered an asset when govt is holding talks with a group which is riding the angst of the student community, as any misstep may inflame passions.Nadda cut his teeth in students' politics as an ABVP activist in Patna and Himachal University and grew in the role to head Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha, the youth wing of BJP, collecting long experience of agitational politics, the second nature of student activism, which makes him the right person for the job.BJP circles are of the view that while being health minister who looked after the treatment of injured protesters put Nadda in a position to connect with CJP, his emergence as a negotiator came as a surprise.It is surmised that the former BJP chief's low-key presence added to his acceptability. A BJP functionary said one of his strengths was that he was soft-spoken but also knew where to draw the line, a trait that ensures that he could engage with protestors skilfully while ensuring that the govt's views were also put across firmly.He had also met activist Sonam Wangchuk in a private hospital as part of govt's efforts to persuade him to break his hunger strike and engage in talks to end the stir.Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, known for his political savvy and proven track record of successful political outreach, could have been the other choice but for the fact that his resignation is CJP's main demand.With some other leading BJP figures not really a good fit for the job because of their seniority, the task fell on Nadda, now a member of the party's brains trust.
Article Summary: Nadda cut his teeth in students' politics as an ABVP activist in Patna and Himachal University. He grew in the role to head Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha, the youth wing of BJP. It is surmised that the former BJP chief's low-key presence added to his acceptability.

Article Title: 'No cases against peaceful protesters': List of govt assurances that ended Sonam Wangchuk's fast
Article Text:
Wangchuk announced the end of his fast after Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh met him at Medanta Hospital in Gurugram around midnight and conveyed the government's assurances.

NEW DELHI: Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Friday ended his 26-day indefinite hunger strike after receiving assurances from the Centre that key demands raised by students protesting over alleged examination irregularities would be addressed.In a post on X, Wangchuk said the government had assured that there would be a discussion in Parliament on accountability in the examination system, compensation for families of students who died by suicide following the recent NEET paper leak, and no cases against peaceful protesters."END OF HUNGER... BEGINNING OF ACCOUNTABILITY...!" Wangchuk wrote.He added, "Sonam Wangchuk ends his fast after 26 days upon getting assurance from the government and members of parliament of all political parties that the issue of accountability in the failing examination system will be discussed on the floors of the Indian Parliament.""The government also gave assurance that families of suicide victims in the recent NEET examination paper leak will be given adequate compensation and that there will be no cases registered against the peacefully protesting students and youths," he said.Wangchuk announced the end of his fast after Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh met him at Medanta Hospital in Gurugram around midnight and conveyed the government's assurances."Just now in the presence of Union Ministers JP Nadda, Dr Jitendra Singh and the senior leaders of Apex Body of Leh Ladakh, I finally broke my fast after 26 days," Wangchuk wrote.He said 65 Members of Parliament from different political parties had either visited him or signed letters urging him to end the fast."This was done after long negotiations on various conditions and in view of possible violence in the country. I will explain the conditions in detail in a separate video very soon. Meanwhile, I urge you all to stay very vigilant about not allowing violence of any kind anywhere," he said.Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed Wangchuk's decision to end the fast. In a post on X, he said, "I urge Sonam ji to follow his daily routine as advised by the doctors and regain his weight as soon as possible.""I pray to the Almighty that Sonam ji remains healthy," the Prime Minister added.The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which has been leading the protest at Jantar Mantar, welcomed Wangchuk's decision but said its agitation would continue until Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns.Wangchuk joined the CJP-led protest on June 28 and began an indefinite hunger strike in support of demands for accountability over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations, reforms to the education system and Pradhan's resignation. During the fast, he lost around 11 kg and continued the protest from Medanta Hospital after being shifted there from Safdarjung Hospital following legal proceedings.
Article Summary: Wangchuk announced the end of his fast after Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh met him at Medanta Hospital in Gurugram. The Cockroach Janta Party welcomed Wangchuk's decision but said its agitation would continue until Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns.

Article Title: Opposition MPs take out march in solidarity with protesters
Article Text:
Opposition MPs stage protest against govt at Parliament in black clothes

NEW DELHI: Opposition MPs took out a 'candlelight march' Thursday to the Gandhi Smriti in solidarity with the protesting students, two days after they held a dharna outside the PM's residence and were forcibly evacuated by police.The MPs belonging to Congress, SP, TMC, Left parties, RJD, Shiv Sena and others met at Rahul Gandhi's residence. From there, they marched to the Gandhi Smriti holding their phone torches. The marchers included Rahul, K C Venugopal, Ramjilal Suman, Supriya Sule, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, N K Premachandran, John Brittas, Sandosh Kumar, Sudhakar Singh, Misa Bharti, Arvind Sawant, Saugata Roy and Mahua Moitra.Rahul said, "We go to remember the students we lost - the children driven to take their own lives after the NEET paper leak. And we go to stand with the students who lie injured today - beaten for peacefully demanding justice and accountability. India's students are not alone. The entire opposition stands with them and their demands."Congress's P Chidambaram said, "All roads are barricaded, and hundreds of policemen are mobilised to 'secure' the roads of Delhi. What is govt afraid of? Why this sense of panic?" Earlier, Congress rubbished PM Modi's statement assuring the protesting youth. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the students don't need platitudes after govt used pellet guns, shock batons and tear gas on them.
Article Summary: Opposition MPs took out a 'candlelight march' Thursday to the Gandhi Smriti in solidarity with the protesting students. The MPs belonging to Congress, SP, TMC, Left parties, RJD, Shiv Sena and others met at Rahul Gandhi's residence. The marchers included Rahul, K C Venugopal, Ramjilal Suman and Supriya Sule.

Article Title: US-Iran conflict expands beyond battlefield as Red Sea attacks open new front
Article Text:
Houthi blockade raises global trade concerns

Rubio warns of rising costs

The US-Iran conflict has expanded beyond direct military strikes between the two sides, with Iranian-aligned militants in Yemen targeting shipping routes in the Red Sea. The development comes as Washington and Tehran continue to escalate military pressure, fuelling concerns that neither side can secure a decisive military advantage through force.The conflict widened this week after Houthi militants in Yemen began striking ships passing through the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, a key Red Sea chokepoint linking the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean. The attacks helped push oil prices above $100 a barrel for the first time in two months on Thursday.The US has also intensified its bombing campaign in Iran, carrying out strikes across the country during the most intense phase of fighting since US President Donald Trump and Israel launched military action against Tehran in late February.On Monday, Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels announced an immediate maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia, saying they would block Saudi-linked shipping through the Bab al-Mandeb Strait in retaliation for the kingdom's blockade of Yemen and a recent attack on Sana'a International Airport.The move threatens a critical route Saudi Arabia uses to bypass disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz by exporting crude through its East-West Pipeline to a Red Sea port.The Bab al-Mandeb Strait carries around 12 per cent of global trade, including nearly a quarter of the world's container traffic moving through the Suez Canal.Any prolonged disruption could force vessels to reroute around South Africa's Cape of Good Hope, adding about 2,700 miles (4,345 km) to voyages between Saudi Arabia and the US, according to the US government.According to The Wall Street Journal, President Trump and senior administration officials have warned that the US could further expand its military campaign, including strikes on a suspected Iranian nuclear facility at Pickaxe Mountain or attacks on Iranian infrastructure in response to Iranian actions in the Strait of Hormuz. Political analyst Abdel-Bari Taher told the Associated Press that Yemen's internal divisions make it especially vulnerable to being drawn deeper into the regional conflict, increasing the risk of a wider war.US secretary of state Marco Rubio earlier said pressure on Tehran would continue, referring to Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi's description of Iran's approach as "an eye for an eye.""The price will continue to get higher every single night until they come to their senses," Rubio told reporters on Thursday at a summit in Manila."The president's policy is a head for an eye," Rubio said. "I mean, honestly, that is what it is going to be." He added that president Trump would decide in the coming days whether to escalate military action further.The conflict is also imposing a mounting financial burden on the US. On Wednesday, US secretary of defense Pete Hegseth said the cost of the ongoing conflict with Iran had reached $37.5 billion, including projected operations and maintenance expenses through the end of the current fiscal year. Speaking before the senate appropriations committee, Hegseth said the estimate was about $8 billion higher than the $29 billion figure cited by the Trump administration in May.Analysts told The Wall Street Journal that while both Washington and Tehran have shown a willingness to intensify the confrontation, neither appears capable of achieving its broader strategic objectives through military means alone."There is an escalatory dynamic now," Alan Eyre, a former senior US diplomat who participated in negotiations with Iran, told The Wall Street Journal. "I don't think the United States administration really has a clear strategic concept of what it is trying to do."
Article Summary: Houthi militants in Yemen have begun striking ships passing through the Bab al- Mandeb Strait. The move threatens a critical route Saudi Arabia uses to bypass disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. The US has also intensified its bombing campaign in Iran, carrying out strikes across the country.

Article Title: 'Arrest me if you want, but I am leaving': Sonam Wangchuk releases video alleging harassment; Safdarjung hospital issues clarification
Article Text:
Wangchuk was shifted to Safdarjung Hospital by Delhi Police on July 18 from the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest site at Jantar Mantar





NEW DELHI: Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Friday night released a video on YouTube describing events from the past few days and sharing footage from the time he was leaving Safdarjung Hospital after the Delhi high court permitted his transfer to Medanta Hospital in Gurgaon.The Safdarjung Hospital administration, however, said the video was recorded before it had received the written order of the high court, according to news agency PTI.Wangchuk was shifted to Safdarjung Hospital by Delhi Police on July 18 from the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest site at Jantar Mantar, where he had been on a hunger strike since June 28 in support of the CJP's demands, including accountability for examination paper leaks and the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.Following directions from the Delhi high court, he was moved to Medanta Hospital on July 21.In the video, Wangchuk is seen arguing with a security personnel at Safdarjung Hospital, alleging that he was being stopped from leaving the premises.He can be heard saying that the authorities should either arrest him or allow him to leave.“You are harassing me... If I die of stress, it will be your responsibility,” Wangchuk says in the video.In another part of the clip, he can be heard saying, “Arrest me if you want, but I am leaving.”Reacting to the video, Safdarjung Hospital authorities said it was "purportedly recorded" by Wangchuk's associates inside the hospital on July 21 in an area where videography is not permitted and was released only on Friday.“The video was reportedly recorded before the hospital administration received the written order of the high court. At that time, Mr Wangchuk insisted on leaving the hospital based on information available in the media.“It is pertinent to note that Mr Wangchuk was handed over to the team of doctors from Medanta Gurgaon on the same day at 6.40pm, immediately after the written order was received by the hospital,” they said.Wangchuk ended his hunger strike late Thursday night at Medanta Hospital in Gurgaon in the presence of his wife Gitanjali Angmo and Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh.The activist said he decided to end the fast after receiving assurances from the government and Members of Parliament across party lines on his key demands related to examination reforms and the protection of peaceful protesters.
Article Summary: Activist Sonam Wangchuk released a video on YouTube describing events from the past few days. Wangchuk was shifted to Safdarjung Hospital by Delhi Police on July 18 from the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest site at Jantar Mantar. He had been on a hunger strike since June 28 in support of the CJP's demands.

Article Title: 'Getting IV drips every morning': CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke diagnosed with typhoid
Article Text:
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke





NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday said he has been diagnosed with typhoid but asserted that the agitation will continue until Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns.In a video message, Dipke thanked CJP supporters, whom he referred to as "cockroaches", for carrying out peaceful protests across the country and credited them for the success of the movement."Hello everyone. As you all know, I was not feeling well for the last few days. So, blood reports have come. And I have been diagnosed with typhoid. And my treatment is going on. I am getting IV drips every morning and evening.""But I really want to thank all the cockroaches who are peacefully protesting all over the country. And you have made this movement so successful. A big big thank you to all. And congratulations to you all for making this movement such a big big success," he added.Despite his illness, Dipke expressed confidence that the protests would achieve their objective, saying the movement would continue until Pradhan steps down.The remarks came as CJP reiterated that it may adopt a "tough stance" if the government does not clarify its position on the resignation of the Union Education Minister.Speaking to reporters, CJP activist Ashutosh Ranka said his meeting with Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh was constructive, but added that the organisation was still awaiting a response on its primary demand."Yesterday's meeting yielded a positive response regarding compensation and legal matters, reaching an in-principle agreement. We hope to receive that written agreement today. However, no concrete decision has been made regarding our main demand. Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.""Mainstream media reports suggest sources are saying Pradhan will not step down. If he does not resign, the government should state it clearly, as there is no point in continuing these meetings. We will then decide on our next steps. If the government continues this approach, we will be forced to take a tough stance," Ranka said.Ranka also criticised the Ministry of Education's recent action against 47 National Testing Agency (NTA) officials, saying responsibility ultimately rests with the Education Minister."We will examine the details, but ultimate accountability lies with the Education Minister, who is directly responsible for the paper leaks and the resulting student suicides. He must resign. While we continue to discuss broader reforms and submitted a charter of demands to the government yesterday, his resignation remains key," he added.The CJP has maintained that while discussions with the government on compensation, legal matters and reforms are progressing, its central demand remains the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan.
Article Summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke says he has been diagnosed with typhoid. Dipke thanks CJP supporters, whom he referred to as "cockroaches" for carrying out peaceful protests across the country. CJP activist Ashutosh Ranka says his meeting with Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh was constructive.

Article Title: 'Credible threat' from Iran proxies forced Trump to switch planes mid-trip: Report
Article Text: US President Donald Trump switched from a new Qatari-donated Boeing 747-8 to the older Air Force One before departing Turkey earlier this month, according to reports. The move came after US officials identified what they described as a "credible threat" from Iranian proxy forces targeting the president.The New York Times reported earlier that the threat emerged while Trump was attending the Nato summit in Ankara. He had arrived aboard the newly inducted Boeing 747-8, gifted by Qatar, which does not have the same advanced defensive systems as the legacy Air Force One aircraft.Citing people familiar with the matter, the report claimed that after US officials detected the threat, the US secret service recommended that Trump change aircraft before leaving Turkey. The report said the intelligence indicated that Iranian proxy forces were targeting Trump himself rather than the aircraft. However, the newer Boeing's comparatively limited defensive capabilities made flying on it a greater security risk.CBS News confirmed the report later on Friday, saying the US secret service decided to switch planes after receiving intelligence about "a credible plot to fire a missile at the plane".Trump flew to Ankara aboard the new Boeing 747-8, a $400 million Boeing 747-8 that the US accepted as a gift from the Qatari government last year and spent months retrofitting to prepare for it to carry the president. However, after the summit concluded, the US president flew from Ankara to the United Kingdom in the old Air Force One, before switching back to the newer plane to complete his trip back to the United States.The decision prompted fresh questions about the security capabilities of the new aircraft. Citing sources familiar with the matter, the broadcaster reported that the older Air Force One is equipped with laser technology to blind incoming missiles, along with systems designed to misdirect incoming munitions and other defensive countermeasures. It added that it remains unclear what defensive systems are installed on the newer Qatari-donated jet.Earlier this month, Trump did not disclose the security reason behind the aircraft switch, saying he would use the older Air Force One "for old time's sake". He also told reporters that the new aircraft already "has a lot of capability" but would be "maxed out" over the next month as additional upgrades were completed.Trump has repeatedly referred to alleged Iranian threats against his life in recent months. He has previously said he left standing orders for the US military to destroy Iran "at levels they've never seen before" if Tehran carried out what he described as longstanding threats to assassinate him.The latest revelations also come as Trump weighs further military action against Iran following the collapse of a recent ceasefire. Speaking to reporters at the White House on Friday, Trump said, "We are talking to them. I ​think they're being ​serious. I think ... they are ‌being ⁠by far the most serious that we've seen them, but ​that doesn't ​mean ⁠we get there. We'll see ​what happens." He added, "We're locked and loaded. We're ready to go."
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump switched from a new Qatari-donated Boeing 747-8 to the older Air Force One. The move came after US officials identified what they described as a "credible threat" from Iranian proxy forces targeting the president. The decision prompted fresh questions about the security capabilities of the new aircraft.

Article Title: 'Intense, highly unpredictable': Over 200,000 evacuated as massive wildfires engulf Spain, France
Article Text:
Spain, France battle devastating wildfires

More than 200,000 people have either fled or been ordered to remain indoors as massive wildfires swept across Spain and France on Friday.The fires prompted Spain to declare a national emergency, while French authorities ordered the complete evacuation, by land and sea, of one of the country's most popular holiday destinations.Authorities in south-west France ordered the evacuation of the Cap Ferret peninsula on the Atlantic coast "village by village" as an "intense, highly unpredictable" wildfire scorched more than 19,000 hectares (47,000 acres) of forest.In Spain, the government declared its first-ever national emergency over a wildfire after two major blazes merged outside Madrid, while a third fire was close to joining them amid extreme heat and tinder-dry conditions across much of southern Europe.Madrid regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso described the blaze as the "worst fire in the history of the region", saying the area was facing a "perfect storm" of high temperatures, relentless winds and converging fire fronts.Local emergency services said the wildfires were advancing towards the municipalities of Robledo de Chavela and Fresnedillas de la Oliva, about 50 kilometres (31 miles) from the Spanish capital."The wildfire is at its peak and is currently beyond the capacity of firefighters to contain," Carlos Novillo, the Madrid regional government's emergency management chief, said, as cited by the BBC."It's not possible to attack the fire in that area, so defensive measures are being taken," he added.A national emergency, which allows Spain's central government to assume powers and responsibilities normally held by the country's autonomous regions, has been declared only once before — during the nationwide blackout in April 2025.In south-west France, around 200,000 people have been evacuated as wildfires tore through the Gironde and Landes regions.In the early hours of Saturday, authorities ordered the precautionary evacuation of four towns near Bordeaux: Saint-Médard-en-Jalles, Saint-Jean-d'Illac, Martignas-sur-Jalles and Saint-Aubin-de-Médoc. According to Le Monde, the four municipalities have a combined population of about 58,400.In 2022, a wildfire in south-west France scorched more than 30,000 hectares and forced the evacuation of 50,000 people. Fueled by dry conditions and strong winds, the latest blazes have swept through coastal pine forests, with flames reaching up to 10 metres (30 feet) high.French president Emmanuel Macron said he had activated the European Union's civil protection mechanism as the country battled multiple wildfires after enduring three successive heatwaves since May.Scientists say climate change is making extreme weather events more frequent and more intense by drying out soils and waterways, fuelling wildfires and contributing to thousands of excess deaths. Europe is warming at nearly twice the global average rate.
Article Summary: Spanish government declares first-ever national emergency over wildfire. French authorities order complete evacuation of one of country's most popular holiday destinations. More than 200,000 people either fled or were ordered to remain indoors as wildfires swept across Spain and France on Friday.

Article Title: Maharashtra TET paper leak: Main accused Bijendra Gupta arrested from Bihar
Article Text:
Maharashtra Police have arrested alleged TET paper leak mastermind Bijendra Gupta (File Photo).





BHIWANDI: The Thane police probing the alleged Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) paper leak case achieved a major breakthrough on Saturday by arresting the alleged mastermind, Bijendra Gupta, after a three-week manhunt. Gupta was apprehended in Bihar along with his associate, Indrajit Singh, taking the total number of arrests in the case to 14.Bijendra is said to be involved in many papers leaks across several states in the country and was arrested earlier but was on bail during which he leaked again TET paper.A police team tracked down the duo during an early morning operation in Bihar and is bringing them to Mumbai. Both accused are expected to be produced before a Bhiwandi court later in the day to seek their custodial interrogation.Deputy Commissioner of Police (Zone II) Pawan Bansod confirmed the arrests to TOI. "Our team had been relentlessly searching for Bijendra Gupta for the past three weeks. We succeeded in arresting him this morning. Along with him, one of his associates, Indrajit Singh, has also been arrested. Both accused are being brought to Mumbai and will be produced before the Bhiwandi court," Bansod said.The case came to light after DCP Bansod received a tip-off a day before the June 28 TET examination that a group was arriving in Bhiwandi to sell leaked question papers.Acting on the information, Kongaon police station team laid a trap and arrested three persons allegedly attempting to sell the leaked papers. The subsequent investigation uncovered a well-organised racket involved in leaking examination papers and facilitating unfair means for candidates.The probe has so far revealed a network allegedly operating across multiple states. During the investigation, police arrested several key accused, including two employees of an Agra-based printing press from where Gupta is suspected to have procured the leaked question papers.Among those arrested earlier is Gupta's wife, Suman Gupta, who was traced to Samastipur in Bihar. Investigators believe she played an active role in the financial transactions and logistical support of the alleged racket. Police have also seized multiple electronic devices, documents and financial records during the investigation.Investigators further revealed that Gupta had allegedly finalised a deal through arrested accused Kapil Dahiya to sell the leaked question papers to a Pune resident, who remains absconding and is the only accused yet to be arrested in the case.Police claim the Pune-based suspect was in contact with nearly 50 teacher aspirants who were willing to purchase the leaked question papers before the examination.Officials said Gupta's arrest is expected to provide crucial leads on the exact source of the leaked papers, the money trail and the possible involvement of additional members of the syndicate.
Article Summary: Bijendra Gupta was apprehended in Bihar along with his associate, Indrajit Singh, taking the total number of arrests in the case to 14. Bijendra is said to be involved in many papers leaks across several states in the country and was arrested earlier but was on bail during which he leaked again TET paper.

Article Title: CJP launches website, invites proof against ‘police excesses’
Article Text:
CJP spokesperson Saurav Das emerges from the meeting with Centre





NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) Friday launched a dedicated website inviting protesters to upload photographs and videos of police personnel who allegedly assaulted demonstrators during and after the July 20 Sansad Chalo march, saying it would identify the officers and pursue legal action against them.Launching the portal at Jantar Mantar, CJP representatives appealed to protesters from across the country to submit visual evidence of the alleged assault.“We will go through every photograph and video, verify them, identify the police personnel involved and file complaints against them. We will demand registration of FIRs against such officers. If FIRs are not registered, we will approach the courts. Lawyers from across the country have come forward to help us and we will obtain court orders to ensure cases are registered,” CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said.He said the organisation will prepare a list of officers allegedly involved in the clampdown and “ensure they are punished till the end”.Besides reiterating its demand for action against the cops allegedly involved, CJP has also sought a public apology from the Delhi police commissioner, Rapid Action Force head and the Centre.“We request that all these demands be accepted at the earliest, failing which the movement will only grow bigger and spread across the country,” CJP said in a letter submitted to Centre Friday.It also sought an assurance that protesters would not be targeted in future, and said in-principal approval for this demand was given by Centre’s representatives who met the CJP spokespersons Friday.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) Friday launched a dedicated website inviting protesters to upload photographs and videos of police personnel who allegedly assaulted demonstrators. CJP representatives appealed to protesters from across the country to submit visual evidence of the alleged assault.

Article Title: NATO-backed scientists planted 13-foot-tall giant grass on war-damaged land near Bucha, hoping its roots can help clean Ukraine's polluted soil
Article Text:
Scientists prepare a field for Miscanthus plants in northern Czech Republic (AFP photo)

Breadbasket of Europe

Poll Vote & Share your view How important is it to develop natural methods for soil restoration in war-affected areas? Very important Not important 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Testing giant Miscanthus

A Ukrainian fighter walks past a burning wheat field (Reuters file photo)

How grass helps soil

Improving soil naturally

A Ukrainian farmer watches as patches of his wheat fields burn (AP file photo)

Research underway in Ukraine

Early findings are encouraging

More than four years of war have left lasting damage across parts of Ukraine. It has not only affected buildings and infrastructure, but also the natural environment. Areas that once supported forests, wildlife and agriculture have been reduced to barren lands which could take years to recover.Ukraine's rich black soil has long been one of the country's biggest strengths. This natural asset helped the European nation become one of the world's leading producers and exporters of grain. Years of war have left it damaged and polluted, making farming difficult in some places.Researchers at the Jan Evangelista Purkyne University (UJEP) in the Czech Republic are testing giant Miscanthus, a fast-growing grass, to see if it can gradually remove harmful pollutants from contaminated soil while also producing biomass that can be used for energy.The research is part of a NATO-backed project that aims to reduce the environmental damage caused by military conflict. Scientists say the process is slow and could take years, but early findings suggest the grass may improve soil health and prepare damaged land for future farming.Ukraine is often called the 'breadbasket of Europe' because of its vast areas of chernozem or black soil. The soil is rich in nutrients and organic matter, making it one of the most fertile soils in the world.It has helped Ukraine become a major producer of wheat, maize and other crops.However, after nearly four-and-a-half years of war, large areas of farmland have been affected by military activity. Soil in some regions has been polluted by oil products, explosives and other contaminants.Heavy vehicles, shelling and fighting have also damaged the land by compacting the soil and destroying vegetation. Restoring this land will be essential if it is to be used for agriculture again.At an experimental site on a former brown coal mine near Most in northern Czech Republic, researchers are growing giant Miscanthus to understand how it behaves in damaged soil."The goal is to revitalise contaminated areas while producing biomass," UJEP environmental scientist Josef Trogl says, as quoted by news agency AFP.Giant Miscanthus is originally from East Asia but is now grown across Europe. It is mainly used as a biomass crop because its dried stems can be burned to produce heat and energy.Researchers believe the plant may also help clean polluted land through a natural process called phytoremediation.Scientists say the plant develops a large and deep root system. These roots can trap some harmful substances, including certain metals and other pollutants, while improving the condition of the soil.Ember Morrissey, a biologist at West Virginia University and co-author of a recent study on giant Miscanthus, says the grass is "capable of growing on degraded and contaminated soils and produces extensive root systems that can accumulate metals while simultaneously restoring soil organic matter."According to the researchers, most of the pollutants remain in the roots underground. The stems and leaves that grow above the ground stay largely clean and can still be harvested as biomass.The plant also improves soil quality in another important way. "The plant also sends up to 40% of organic material it produces through photosynthesis to the soil via its roots, which is way more than other farm plants," Trogl said.Photosynthesis is the process by which plants use sunlight to turn carbon dioxide and water into food, releasing oxygen as a by-product. As giant Miscanthus grows, its deep roots store large amounts of carbon in the soil. Scientists say this helps restore soil organic matter and gradually improves soil health over time.Healthy soil contains organic matter called humus, which helps retain water and nutrients needed for plant growth. Trogl says giant Miscanthus encourages the formation of humus more effectively than many other crops."The development of humus and soil fertility is better here than under other plants," he said, adding that the grass also supports soil microorganisms to faster degrade organic pollutants such as petroleum.Soil microorganisms are tiny living organisms, including bacteria and fungi, that naturally break down harmful substances. By creating better conditions for these organisms, the plant may help speed up the recovery of contaminated land.The Czech research is not limited to laboratory testing. Since 2023, scientists have also been growing giant Miscanthus in Vorzel, near Bucha, a suburb of Kyiv.The area was occupied by Russian forces between February and March 2022 before being liberated the following month. It was later cleared of mines during autumn 2022.According to Valentina Pidlisnyuk, a Ukraine-born professor at UJEP who leads the research team, the land suffered extensive environmental damage."The area was occupied by Russian troops between February and March 2022, liberated in April 2022, and subsequently demined in autumn 2022," she said.Although the grass takes several years to show its full impact, scientists say the first results are positive. Pidlisnyuk said analyses carried out so far have shown positive effects on soil biological parameters and carbon sequestration.Carbon sequestration means capturing and storing carbon in the soil instead of releasing it into the atmosphere. This not only improves soil quality but can also help reduce the amount of carbon dioxide contributing to climate change.Researchers say the project is giving them valuable information about how damaged land can be restored using natural methods instead of relying only on expensive engineering solutions.Worth €346,000 (around $395,000), the project involves researchers from the Czech Republic, Ukraine, Canada, Croatia, Kazakhstan and the United States. It is currently scheduled to continue until next year.
Article Summary: Ukraine's rich black soil has long been one of the country's biggest strengths. Years of war have left it damaged and polluted, making farming difficult in some places. Scientists are testing giant Miscanthus, a fast-growing grass, to see if it can remove harmful pollutants from contaminated soil.

Article Title: Trump confirms Netanyahu's US visit next week amid regional tensions
Article Text:
Trump's remark came in his speech at the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner on Friday.

United States President Donald Trump said that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will visit the US next week as the American forces continue to pound parts of Iran after peace talks fizzled out despite weeks of talks and signing of the MoU between Washington and Tehran.Trump's remark came in his speech at the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner on Friday.Netanyahu and Trump agreed to meet in the United States a few weeks ago following a phone conversation. During the call, Netanyahu congratulated Trump on the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States and praised the close relationship between the two countries.It comes as the US-Israeli war with Iran has again escalated following a breakdown earlier this month of a ceasefire reached as part of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed by the US and Iran.Israel had opposed the agreement from the outset, while its continuing military operations in Lebanon repeatedly threatened diplomatic efforts in the region.The Trump administration has also been mediating separate talks between Israel and Lebanon aimed at ending hostilities. The negotiations do not involve Hezbollah.Both sides have accepted a proposal under which Israeli-held areas in southern Lebanon would eventually be handed over to the Lebanese military.However, there has been little visible progress on the ground since March.During a meeting with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun earlier this week, Trump did not indicate when Israeli forces would withdraw from the occupied areas.Meanwhile, the US military said its Central Command had completed a 13th straight night of strikes against targets in Iran.Iran has continued to respond with attacks on US military assets across the region. Last week, a strike on a US base in Jordan killed three American soldiers.The United States has also increased its military deployment in Israel, a move that some analysts believe could signal preparations for a wider regional escalation.Netanyahu's visit will also take place as Israel's military campaign in Gaza continues. Despite a US-backed ceasefire announced last October, Israeli forces have continued issuing evacuation orders and carrying out frequent strikes across the territory.
Article Summary: Netanyahu and Trump agreed to meet in the United States a few weeks ago following a phone conversation. It comes as the US-Israeli war with Iran has again escalated following a breakdown earlier this month of a ceasefire reached as part of a Memorandum of Understanding.

Article Title: Cockroach rally in Kolkata, without a tail: Protesters, cops clash after 1.5-hour, 3-km march
Article Text:
The Kolkata leg of the nationwide students’ protests on Friday lasted 1.5 hours and covered a 3-odd-km stretch. (PTI Photo)





KOLKATA: The Kolkata leg of the nationwide students’ protests on Friday lasted 1.5 hours and covered a 3-odd-km stretch, bringing the city centre to a grinding halt for over five hours. Without getting into comparison, this was the single biggest rally not called by any mainstream political party in recent times.However, what initially was a peaceful protest took a dramatic turn in the evening after the protesters reached Dorina Crossing in Esplanade and carried out a sit-in. Shoes, lathis and water bottles were hurled at the police. The cops charged back with batons, stopping short of using any force.From the morning, a large cross-section of protesters — mostly Gen Z from not just the city but cutting across south Bengal, the young salaried class, the gig workers and even the pension-holders — responded to the call by eight Left student and youth organisations and the Cockroach Janta Party (Kolkata Chapter) to demand central minister Dharmendra Pradhan ’s resignation over the NEET paper leak while also seeking the dissolution of the National Testing Agency (NTA) and justice for students allegedly subjected to police action during protests in Delhi.By 3 pm, the Sealdah station area and the adjoining Metro station and the mall were overflowing. Both lanes of the busy AJC Bose Road were shut as hundreds of youngsters converged from all corners to join the rally.As a set of 500-odd protesters crossed RR Dental College gate, the cops stopped them briefly to allow an Ultorath procession to pass by. By 3.30 pm, thousands of heads were spotted marching towards Esplanade. Till 5 pm, they came in all forms — some shouting slogans, others singing songs of change. In every hand were placards seeking an array of demands — not just the resignation of Pradhan, but scrapping of the NTA and bringing wide changes in the education sector.Lamiya Firdausi participated in the protest with her two children. “My two kids are grown up but still I have chosen to hit the streets for the future generation. For the past few years, education in our country has taken a back seat and we want a reform in the education system. It should be transparent and corruption-free.”Asutosh College student Anushka Ghosh said: “The protest is in solidarity with the students at Jantar Mantar. We want Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign. What enrages us is that there is no accountability from the govt. The protesters wanted to initiate a dialogue but they were brutally lathi-charged by Delhi Police.” AJC Bose College student Md Faisal echoed the same sentiment. “We are on the streets to fight for our future and question what is going wrong in the country. ”As the rally entered SN Banerjee Road, protesters shouted slogans — ‘Amra kara? GenZ’, ‘Rastaye kara? GenZ’. Azadi slogans filled the air. Placards with deep-rooted, hard-hitting meaning as well as humorous statements — such as ‘Fix the System, Not the Narrative’, ‘Melody Khao, Mera Future Nahi’, ‘Dear Govt: Ctrl+Z, Undo the System’. As the rally moved towards Esplanade, the energy of the crowd doubled. Several protesters carried posters of Sonam Wangchuk and condemned the police brutality.Trouble erupted after the protesters reached Esplanade and blocked all crossings. Police tried to remove them from Dorina Crossing, leading to a scuffle. As a result, the entire area remained blocked for over five hours. The protesters were supposed to join a night vigil in Esplanade but the cops did not grant them permission. Around 6.30 pm, the protesters moved to Rani Rashmoni Avenue and planned to organise the night vigil there till 2 am. Around 9.15 pm, the police dispersed them from there “peacefully”, asking them to apply afresh for staging a night protest. They removed the guard rails and opened the road for traffic movement.Deeptaru Saha, a protester and SFI supporter, said: “We had planned to stay here till 2 am for the protest. However, the cops asked us to leave the road. We followed their instruction but our protest will continue.” Akash Kar, central executive committee member of SFI, said: “After today’s success, the protests will continue in different colleges, universities and localities from Saturday. We will continue to fight for students. ”Meanwhile, the Trinamool Chhatra Parishad has called for a protest from Paddapukur to Moulali on Saturday. Reclaim the Night Women Trans Queer United has plans to go to Delhi Jantar Mantar and support the students’ protest there. They would join as allies to student movement calls made in future.Accusations surfaced from student bodies, especially the SFI and AISA, that “outsiders” aligned to ABVP had plotted the disturbances. ABVP denied the charges, saying no one from the organisation was anywhere near the venue and stated they will mull legal action for trying to defame them.Lalbazar stated that specific cases will be drawn up regarding Friday’s incidents at Esplanade even as CCTV footage is being checked thoroughly. “We have detained a few individuals and whether they have any links with the protesters is being established,” said a senior cop.
Article Summary: The Kolkata leg of the nationwide students’ protests on Friday lasted 1.5 hours and covered a 3-odd-km stretch. This was the single biggest rally not called by any mainstream political party in recent times. The protesters were supposed to join a night vigil in Esplanade but the cops did not grant them permission.
